corrected_verdict: NOVEL_AS_FAR_AS_FOUND. The specific K* values and s-switch points are the paper's own computations. The mechanism behind the switches is standard L_q (q<1) concave minimisation over a polyhedron, which is known, and the programme is equivalent to maximising the spectral gap of a weighted circulant graph on Z_p.
issues:
No prior computation of these numbers found. Known maths the checker did not flag:

(1) Minimisers being vertices of P_p (the basis of prop:shapes and the p=13/23 switch points) is standard L_q sparse minimisation. Jiang-Ye preprint, Theorem 3: the basic feasible solutions of min sum x_j^p s.t. Ax=b, x>=0, 0<p<1, are exactly its local minimisers. This is published as Ge-Jiang-Ye, Math. Program. 129:285-299 (2011). Cite it beside the self-contained proof in app:shape.

(2) The programme's coverage sum_j y_j(1-cos 2pi j delta/p) is half the Laplacian eigenvalue of the weighted circulant (Cayley) graph on Z_p. So Gamma_s(p) is a max algebraic connectivity under an L_{1/s} weight budget, and M_K(p) is the same quantity for K-generator circulants. The paper cites Alon-Roichman but never states this reading. An optional sentence would pre-empt spectral-graph reviewers. The only hit for circulant algebraic-connectivity maximisation was arXiv:2110.01918 (unweighted, no tables), so the numbers are not anticipated.

All four confirmed citations re-verified from the texts:
- Nanda: {14,35,41,42,52}, five of six non-zero. The ICLR venue could not be re-checked (OpenReview login wall).
- Chughtai (PMLR 202:6243-6267, page fetched): Table 5 C113 MLP 13/11/15/10; Table 6 transformer 3/4/4/3.
- Zhong: p=59, circles 17/3/44, 91.4%.
- McCracken 2505.18266: the true title and authors are 'Uncovering a Universal Abstract Algorithm for Modular Addition in Neural Networks', Gavin McCracken et al. The refs.bib entry (wrong title, 'Andrew') must be fixed.

Minor: do not cite Zhong for the '3-7' range. Zhong reports 3 circles at p=59 (6 with accompanying circles).

The heuristic flags stand:
- every cell is certified only for K<=Kmax;
- (113,3)=7 is above the exhaustive range, and the equal-share value is 5;
- 'Table gives the counts' should say 'computed counts'.

extra_citations.why: Theorem 3 of the preprint says the local minimisers of L_p (0<p<1) minimisation over {Ax=b, x>=0} are exactly the basic feasible solutions (vertices). This is the known fact behind prop:shapes(i) and the finitely-many-switches mechanism that produces the p=13 and p=23 switch points. The published metadata was verified on Crossref.
